correctness.rationale: After one-sided deletions only N=2u²,u²+v²,2v² can fail, since every other representation has a retained root. For split deletions, reorienting distinct roots avoids the mismatched forbidden positions, so only 2u² and 2v² obstruct. Jacobi r_2(N)=4P(N) for N known representable by two squares; diagonal (t,t) has exactly four signed ordered representations and distinct (u,v) has eight. Other unordered representations exist precisely at P(2t²)>1 (equivalent to a split prime in t) and P(u²+v²)>2. Coprime (5,37) and CRT class v≡0 mod13,1 mod5,3 mod17,4 mod41 supply infinitely many witnesses with no common prime. Independent oracle enumerated all 3160 pairs u<v<=80 and their critical unordered square representations, agreeing with both criteria.

final_claim: Let S be nonnegative integer squares, 1<=u<v, delta(t)=1 iff a prime congruent 1 mod4 divides t, P(N)=product over p=1mod4 dividing N of (ord_p(N)+1). Split holes: (S\{u^2})+(S\{v^2})=S+S iff delta(u)=delta(v)=1. Joint holes: (S\{u^2,v^2})+S=S+S iff both delta values equal 1 and P(u^2+v^2)>=3. The conditions differ at (5,13); infinitely many coprime same-factor pairs occur by the given CRT progression.
limitations: Only two distinct positive square holes and two allocation patterns; arbitrary finite or infinite removed square sets not covered.
